title: Currency pairs: base and quote

inOneLine.simple: A forex price tells you how much of one currency you need to buy one unit of another.
inOneLine.balanced: Every forex quote is a [[currency-pair]]: the price of one unit of the [[base-currency]] expressed in the [[quote-currency]].

explain.simple: In forex you always swap one currency for another, so prices come in pairs, like EUR/USD. The first currency (EUR) is the base. The second (USD) is the quote. The number shows how many US dollars one euro costs. If you buy EUR/USD, you buy euros and pay with dollars. If you sell EUR/USD, you sell euros and receive dollars.
explain.balanced: A [[currency-pair]] such as EUR/USD is read as 'one unit of the [[base-currency]] costs this many units of the [[quote-currency]]'. Buying the pair means going long the base and short the quote; selling means the opposite. When the price rises, the base has strengthened against the quote.
explain.advanced: A forex quote is an exchange rate between two currencies. Long EUR/USD is economically long EUR and short USD. Profit and loss are first measured in the quote currency and must be converted into your account currency when the two differ.

assumptions: Ignore spread and costs for now
steps: To buy 1,000 EUR you need 1,000 × 1.1000 = 1,100 USD.
If EUR/USD rises to 1.1100, those 1,000 EUR are worth 1,110 USD: the euro strengthened against the dollar.
Here USD is the base and JPY is the quote: 1 US dollar costs 150 Japanese yen.
If USD/JPY falls to 148.00, one dollar buys fewer yen: the dollar weakened against the yen.

explainSimpler: EUR/USD = 1.1000 means: one euro costs 1.10 dollars. Buying the pair means buying euros.
commonMistake: Reading the pair backwards. In EUR/USD the price is in dollars per euro, not euros per dollar. If you buy expecting the dollar to get stronger, you have the trade the wrong way round.

quickCheck.prompt: In GBP/USD, which currency is the base?

options.explanation: Right: the first currency in the pair is the base.
No: USD is second, so it is the quote currency the price is measured in.

quickCheck.prompt: EUR/USD moves from 1.1000 to 1.0900. What happened?

options.text: The euro weakened against the dollar
options.explanation: Right: one euro now buys fewer dollars.

options.text: The euro strengthened against the dollar
options.explanation: No: a lower price means one euro is worth fewer dollars.
No: the price of a euro in dollars fell.

doItNow.instructions: Write down three currency pairs you have seen. For each one, name the base and the quote currency, and say what 'buying' that pair means.
